plan: This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price is my own sealed bid. In such auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy—bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. This auction structure effectively functions as a second-price (Vickrey) auction, since the winner pays the second-highest bid regardless of their own bid amount, as long as they bid above it. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value, while bidding lower risks losing an item I could profit from. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $16 to maximize expected profit.

This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a low value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $24, I should bid exactly $24 to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot game.
